title: Containers: Registry, Instances and Container Apps

header.html: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources (20-25%)
Create and manage an Azure container registry; provision a container by using Azure Container Instances; provision a container by using Azure Container Apps; manage sizing and scaling for containers
the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 study guide, skills measured as of October 26, 2023

html:
1Containers in one page

A container packages an application and its dependencies so it runs the same everywhere. It shares the host OS kernel, so it starts fast and is lighter than a VM. A container image is the template; a container registry stores images.

2Azure Container Registry (ACR)

Azure Container Registry is a private registry for container images (Docker format) and artifacts.

Topic Fact
SKUs Basic, Standard, Premium; Premium adds geo-replication, private endpoints and content trust
Push and pull docker login <name>.azurecr.io, then docker push and docker pull
Authentication Microsoft Entra identity (recommended), service principal, managed identity, or the admin account (for testing)
ACR Tasks Build images in Azure (on commit, on base image update, on a schedule)
Roles AcrPull, AcrPush for access
Exam tip

. "Replicate the registry to several regions" = ACR Premium with geo-replication. Avoid the admin account in production.

3Azure Container Instances (ACI)

ACI runs containers directly on Azure with no VM or orchestrator to manage. It is the fastest and simplest way, billed per second.

Topic Fact
Container group Several containers sharing a lifecycle, network and storage on one host (like a pod)
Size CPU and memory are set when you create the group; to change, recreate it
Networking Public IP and DNS name label, or VNet deployment (private)
Restart policy Always, OnFailure, Never (use Never or OnFailure for batch jobs)
Storage Mount Azure Files shares for persistent data

Use for: simple apps, batch jobs, build agents, bursts. Not for: long-running microservices needing autoscale and ingress (use Container Apps).

4Azure Container Apps

Azure Container Apps is a serverless platform for microservices and containerized apps (built on Kubernetes with no cluster management).

Feature Fact
Environment A secure boundary (VNet, logging) that hosts several container apps
Revisions Immutable versions; traffic splitting for blue/green or canary
Ingress HTTP/HTTPS external or internal endpoint
Autoscale KEDA rules (HTTP requests, queue length, CPU, memory, custom) and scale to zero
Replicas Set minimum and maximum; each replica gets the CPU and memory you assign
Exam tip

. "Run a containerized microservice that scales on queue length and can scale to zero, without managing Kubernetes" = Azure Container Apps. "Run one container quickly with no scaling logic" = ACI.

5Sizing and scaling

Service Sizing Scaling
ACI CPU and memory per container at creation No built-in autoscale; create more groups
Container Apps CPU and memory per replica Min/max replicas and scale rules
Exam tip

. Container Apps = serverless microservices with scale rules; ACI = a quick container group; ACR = the image store.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A company wants to store private container images and replicate them across regions. Which service and SKU fit?

  • AAzure Container Instances
  • BAzure Blob Storage
  • CAzure Container Registry Premium
  • DAzure Backup
Show the answer

Answer: C. Geo-replication is a Premium feature of ACR.

S2A team wants to run a short batch container without managing servers and pay per second. What fits?

  • AA Virtual Machine Scale Set
  • BAn App Service plan
  • CAzure Container Instances
  • DAzure SQL
Show the answer

Answer: C. ACI runs containers on demand with per-second billing.

S3A microservice should scale from zero based on queue length. What should be used?

  • AAzure Container Instances
  • BAn availability set
  • CA single VM
  • DAzure Container Apps
Show the answer

Answer: D. Container Apps supports KEDA rules and scale to zero.

S4How can CPU and memory of a container group in ACI be changed?

  • ARecreate the container group with new values
  • BEdit them live in the portal while the container group runs
  • CUse autoscale rules on the container group CPU
  • DResize the virtual network that hosts the container group
Show the answer

Answer: A. ACI resources are set at creation.

S5Which ACI restart policy fits a batch job that should not restart after success?

  • AAlways
  • BHybrid
  • COnFailure or Never
  • DRolling
Show the answer

Answer: C. Batch jobs use OnFailure or Never.

S6Which Container Apps feature allows traffic to be split between versions?

  • ARevisions
  • BRegistries
  • CAvailability zones
  • DSAS tokens
Show the answer

Answer: A. Revisions are immutable versions with traffic splitting.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does ACR store?

Show the answer

Container images and artifacts.

R2What is a container group in ACI?

Show the answer

Containers sharing a lifecycle, network and storage on one host.

R3What engine does Container Apps use for scale rules?

Show the answer

KEDA.

R4Can Container Apps scale to zero?

Show the answer

Yes.

R5Which ACR SKU supports geo-replication?

Show the answer

Premium.

R6How is ACI billed?

Show the answer

Per second of CPU and memory used.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
ACR Basic/Standard/Premium; Premium geo-replication; ACR Tasks; Entra auth
ACI quickest, no orchestrator, container groups, fixed size, per-second billing
Container Apps serverless microservices, revisions, ingress, KEDA autoscale, scale to zero
